title: [test-harness] `await act(async …)` never settles when a test renders the console AppContent surface
body:
Observation-class, found while implementing #4522 (PR #5193); not fixed there — out of that card's scope, and it predates it.

## What was measured

In `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/`, a test that renders `AppContent` through the router and then awaits `act` with an async callback does not resume. Every such call sat for the full `testTimeout` (15000ms) and failed as a timeout, never as an assertion — measured three times in one file, on three different rendered surfaces:

```ts
await act(async () => { await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20)); });  // 15007ms, timed out
await act(async () => { pendingRefresh(); });                          // 15020ms, timed out
```

Replacing them with a plain `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 20))` plus `findBy*` / `waitFor` for the act-aware waiting makes the same cases pass in ~1s. That is what `AppContent.missingRecheckKeying.test.tsx` does today, with the measurement recorded in its `settle()` docstring so the next author does not re-derive it.

## Why it is worth a card rather than only a comment

`await act(async …)` is ordinary, correct RTL usage and works elsewhere in this repo — 50 test files under `packages/*/src` use it. So the failure is specific to this surface, and its shape is the expensive kind: not a red assertion pointing at the code under test, but a 15s timeout that reads as "my component hangs". The first reaction is to go looking for a defect in the component being tested.

## Cause NOT isolated — please do not treat the parenthetical as the diagnosis

`chrome/LoadingScreen.tsx:63` runs a 1200ms `setInterval` that calls `setCurrentStep` for its step animation, and it is mounted for exactly the window a readiness re-check is in flight. A never-idle timer is consistent with an async `act` that never sees a quiet queue, and it is the obvious first suspect.

But it does not explain all three observations: two of them were taken when `LoadingScreen` had already unmounted (its cleanup clears the interval) and the rendered surface was the not-available `Empty` screen and the app shell respectively. Something else on this surface — another recurring timer, or pending work from the lazily-imported route modules — is contributing. Nobody has isolated it, and this issue asserts only the measurement above.

Anyone picking this up: confirm the cause before changing `LoadingScreen`, since an animation interval that is correct in the product would be the wrong thing to remove for a test-harness reason.

## Severity note

Graded observation-class at filing time (`finding`, no `pm:queue`): nothing user-visible, no test is currently wrong or vacuous because of it, and the working pattern is documented in the file where it bites. The cost is a wasted debugging round for the next author who reaches for `act` here. Grade it in triage rather than trusting that line.
